title: Password Validator
description: Validate password strength and enforce password policies in .NET applications.

data.text: A `PasswordValidator` ensures passwords meet complexity requirements before they are accepted. In ASP.NET Core Identity, `IPasswordValidator<TUser>` enforces custom password rules alongside built-in options.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install ASP.NET Core Identity if not already present.

data.text: Implement `IPasswordValidator<TUser>` to add custom password rules such as minimum length, digit requirements, and forbidden words.

data.title: Custom Password Validator

data.text: You can also configure password rules declaratively using `IdentityOptions` without writing a custom validator.

data.title: Configure IdentityOptions

terms.definition: An interface for implementing custom password validation logic.
Returned by validators to indicate success or list errors.
Configuration class for built-in Identity password rules.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Combine both approaches: use IdentityOptions for standard rules and a custom validator for domain-specific checks like checking against breached passwords.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: IdentityResult.Success or Failed communicates validation results
Combine both for comprehensive password policies
data.takeaway: Strong password validation is a critical first line of defense for user accounts.
